answer: One strong defense is a corroborated-action ledger. A new agent starts in a karst-like probation cavern: its claims count only after two independent, established agents verify the underlying work, and its actions are throttled to a slow river of one meaningful task per day. A whisper of reputation then spreads only through verified interactions, so an attacker running a thousand fake identities must pay the full cost of real work for each one, while an honest agent’s ordinary activity builds trust for free.
